segments.text: So I got a call from your office about my blood work, the kidney number was up, and I'm here because, uh, they said it might be the pills I take for my back.
That's right. Your creatinine came back higher than last time, and I want to talk through why. Let's start with the back. How long has it been bothering you?
The back pain? Three months. No, sorry, four months. It started when I was moving my sister's couch in the spring, or maybe the summer, anyway.
Four months of back pain. And is it constant, or does it come and go?
Mostly it's there when I bend. Tying my boots is the worst part of the day.
Okay. Tell me what you take for it. Be honest, nobody's grading you.
Ibuprofen. The 600 mg ones, I take them two or three times a day. Well, two, usually, but three on the bad days. I've got a bottle in the truck, one in the kitchen, one in my jacket.

Right. Here's the plain version of what that does. Your kidneys are like a coffee filter, and they need a steady flow of blood to work. Ibuprofen squeezes down the little pipes feeding the filter, so it clogs up a bit.
Huh. So it's the pills doing it, not the back.
The pills are the likely culprit, yes. From what I'm seeing, it looks like the anti-inflammatories are straining your kidneys. It's early, and it's usually reversible.
Reversible. That's the good word. How early?
Well, your number is up, but you're not in trouble yet. That's why I wanted you in. Any blood in your urine? Dark, or red, or like tea?
No. Nothing like that. It's yellow like always. Well, darker in the morning, but everybody's is.
That's normal. Do you remember if anyone ever told you about your kidneys before?
I get kidney stones, every few years. I passed one on a fishing trip once, worst day of my life.
That's helpful to know. Anything else on your medical history, the sort of thing you'd say if someone asked you?
High blood pressure. I'm supposed to watch it. Oh, and I had my appendix out as a teenager, you were going to ask that.
I was heading there. Appendix as a teenager. What do you do for work, with that back?
Construction. Framing houses, I've done it for twenty-two years. No, twenty-three. Whichever, long enough.
Heavy on the back, that explains it. And any alcohol?
A beer or two after work. Weekends maybe four.
Okay. Let me get your blood pressure and pulse while we're talking.
Blood pressure is 138 over 84, and your pulse is 70. Not bad at all.
Better than last time, I think. I forgot to take my coffee this morning, that probably helps.
Fewer cups never hurts. So, here's the plan. I'd like to repeat the creatinine blood test, so we can see whether the number is moving. I'll order that today.
Do I have to fast again?
No fasting needed. I'd also like a urine test, to check whether any protein is leaking through the filter.
Same as last time, the little cup?
The little cup. You can leave both at the lab on the way out.
Okay. And what do I do about the back? I can't just not take anything.
Stop the ibuprofen, all of it, including the bottle in the truck. Use heat on the back in the evening, keep moving, and I'll have the physiotherapist's number for you at the desk.
The bottle in the truck. Yeah. Fine. I'll bring it in the house and throw it out.
Good. Also, check labels on cold and flu medicines, because a lot of them contain similar stuff.
Got it. I never thought about the cold stuff.
Most people don't. Any other questions for me?
Just the one thing, what was it, oh, can I still lift at work?
Lift with your legs, keep loads close to your body, and listen to the back. If it screams, put it down.
Ha, the back screams plenty. Thanks, doc.
Anytime. Look after those kidneys.
